newsitem.title: UK: OVER-PRODUCTION HITS STAINLESS STEEL PRICE - BROKER.
newsitem.headline: OVER-PRODUCTION HITS STAINLESS STEEL PRICE - BROKER.

text.p: Stainless steel prices have been undermined by over-production by European producers and over-stocking by buyers, brokers Macquarie Equities said in a report on Monday.
"Plans by the European stainless mills to raise prices during the rest of this year have been thwarted by a downturn in prices," the report said.
Base price quotations in Germany were at the equivalant of $1,480 per tonne, down 5.4 percent from June's quote, it said.
"The reason for the price weakness is massive over-production by European stainless steel producers and over-stocking by buyers," Macquarie added.
The broker estimated European melted stainless steel output rose by 15.4 percent year-on-year in the first half of 1997.

The largest rises among European countries were recorded in Sweden with a January-June rise of 28.3 percent, Spain with a January-May rise of 21 percent and Finland with a estimated 25 percent rise in January-June.
European order backlogs remain long with no plans to cut production in the third quarter of the year.
But fourth-quarter cuts are seen possible if the price continues to weaken and if the trend in Germany to trim orders spreads to other countries.
Outside of Europe production was up strongly year-on-year in South Africa, South Korea and Taiwan, while Japanese and U.S. output has been more subdued.

Meanwhile the price of three months nickel was hovering around $7,000 per tonne, which was up from the year's low of $6,420 in January but well off the high of $8,325 in March. Nickel is mainly used in the manufacture of stainless steel.
